messages:
Maria G: Heads-up — I ran a short sim this morning for cold-start-heavy traffic in eu-west1. Wanted to share the numbers and get thoughts on a hysteresis admission rule before we lock the weekend config.

Aj Patel: Nice. What's the baseline and the surge profile you used?

Maria G: Baseline qps steady-state is ~450 r/s for the model pool; expected burst pattern is 3x for ~30-45min windows, 2x for the rest of the hour (based on last 3 weeks). I used GPU-hours baseline 17.2k/week and winter surge +40% -> 24.1k/week.

Simon L: Did you model cold-start penalty? That's the kicker for p99 when scale-up happens.

Maria G: Yup — added a 750ms cold-start penalty per warmup for the first N replicas (N depends on prewarm config). Lookup: cold_start_ms = 750 * min(1, (replicas_provisioned / replicas_needed) ).

Li Chen: What SLOs are we targeting for this pool? p95/p99?

Maria G: Target p95 < 250ms, p99 < 900ms (for interactive routes). For batch/rerank we allow higher p99 but separate pool.

Aj Patel: Old admit policy (step) flapped last Nov during the EU outage. Any smoothing logic we can apply to avoid oscillation?

Maria G: I prototyped a damped admit rate:
```
admit_rate_t = clip(admit_rate_{t-1} + k * (desired_util - observed_util), 0, max_admit)

where k = 0.15 during normal ops, 0.05 in coldstart windows (first 20m after scale events)
```
This prevents sharp admits when observed_util suddenly drops due to network blips.

Simon L: Makes sense. How about hysteresis thresholds? We should require util < 65% for 2 consecutive 30s buckets before scale-down. Scale-up can be more aggressive.

Maria G: Exactly what I tested — scale-up when util > 80% for 2 buckets, scale-down when util < 65% for 4 buckets. Added a cooldown of 3 minutes between decisions. Reduced flapping in sim by ~70%.

Li Chen: Any cost tradeoffs? More prewarm -> better p99 but higher idle GPU-hours. Numbers?

Maria G: Short numbers from the sim: with 12 prewarm replicas we hit target p99 95% of the time during peaks but weekly GPU-hours rose from 24.1k to 26.8k (~11% increase). With 6 prewarm replicas p99 misses doubled but cost was flat.

Aj Patel: Could we combine tiny prewarm + admission smoothing to hit both cost and SLOs?

Maria G: Yes — the sweet spot in the sim was 8 prewarms + k dampening at 0.1. That gave p99 <900ms 88% of peak windows and only +4% GPU-hours vs baseline surge plan.

oncall-bot: Incident replay scheduled for eu-west1 cold-start spike analysis — link: https://ci/replay/2060123456

Simon L: Does the plan require cross-region fallback? If eu-west1 capacity saturates, can we route to eu-north with acceptable latency?

Maria G: We tested soft-fallback (route <20% traffic to eu-north when admit_block activated). Latency penalty ~120ms median, p99 penalty ~250ms but still within a tolerable band for non-interactive jobs. For interactive we keep fallback <10%.

Li Chen: Any network constraints from inter-region egress costs? That 20% cross-route will add ~6% to bandwidth bill for EU. Ops okay?

Aj Patel: Finance OK'd up to 8% extra egress for surge protections last quarter, but we'd need an emergency approval for 6% if sustained. Document the expected duration if we flip fallback for >2 hours.

Maria G: Will add to the runbook. Action items: (1) roll k-damped admit to canary (10% traffic) tonight, (2) add fallback caps by model-route, (3) update runbook with cost delta and emergency approval steps.

Simon L: +1. Please include the sim script and parameter file in the PR so we can tweak fast.

Maria G: Posting sim gist in the PR in ~30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
